fields.features_heading: What a PIP Needs After the Meeting Ends
fields.features_subheading: Describe the plan you run, and Emergent writes the form plus the record HR opens on the end date.
fields.feature_1:
Goals saved only with a number and a date

Write a vague goal such as better call quality and the form asks for the measure, the target, and the due date before saving it. Both people know on day one what meeting it means.
fields.feature_2:
The current result beside the expected one

Each concern takes two values: where the employee stands today and the standard the role expects. The gap reads as a number on the plan, not as an adjective in a paragraph.
fields.feature_3:
A log of the support the company promised

List the training, shadowing, or weekly one-on-ones the plan offers. The manager records each session as it happens. A week with no session shows as a blank row on the plan record.
fields.feature_4:
Check-in reminders that carry only a link

The manager gets an email before each scheduled check-in. It holds a link to the plan and nothing else. Goals and scores stay out of every inbox and every shared channel.
fields.feature_5:
Signed by the employee and the manager

Both people sign the plan on a phone or a laptop when it starts, and again when it closes. The employee also gets a comments box of their own, saved with the signed record.
fields.feature_6:
Your plan records, exportable as code

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and run the form next to the HR system you already use. Each plan and its final outcome stay in tables you own.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a Plan Gets Used, Week by Week
fields.tab_content_1:
For a sales goal to save, it needs a number and a date

Dana Kilburn writes a 60-day plan for rep #207 at Garnock Office Supply. Her first goal reads book more demos, and the form will not save it. She rewrites it as 8 booked demos a month, then adds 50 logged calls a week as the second goal. Each one carries its own due date before the plan goes to the rep.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two coaching sessions a week, each one logged

Agent #3318 started a plan at Hattersley Software with a QA score of 71 and a target of 85. The plan promises 2 coaching sessions a week with team lead Joel Ravenscroft. He logs each session with its date and the calls they reviewed. By week 3 the score is 78, and all 6 sessions are on the record.
fields.tab_content_3:
An email 2 days ahead of each check-in

Every other Thursday, supervisor Nadia Truscott meets picker #1046 at Cobbridge Logistics. Two days before each meeting she gets an email that links to the plan and shows no details from it. At the week 4 check-in she opens the link and marks the error goal met: 3 picking errors in 2 weeks against a limit of 4.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 7 open plans, the one past its end date

Gail Wainscott runs HR for the 4 stores of Vintry Pharmacy and sees all 7 open plans in one view, sorted by end date. Two of them end this week. One ended 3 days ago with no outcome recorded. It sits at the top in red until the store manager closes it.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a PIP Form Template
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a PIP form template whose goals can be counted, checked on a schedule, and closed with an outcome.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the gap you have seen
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Turn each concern into a goal
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 List the support you will provide
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start from the gap between the work you see and the work the role needs. Write down each concern with dates and examples, such as 4 shipping deadlines missed in March. Each concern becomes its own section of the form, with room for the evidence.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write each goal so the employee can hit it and you can count it. Give it a unit, a target, and a deadline inside the plan window. A goal with any of those missing stays a draft. Nobody signs a plan that cannot be judged.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the current result next to each goal, pulled from the same report you will measure with later. A rep booking 4 demos a month against a target of 8 is judged on that one report at every check-in, not on a fresh impression.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the coaching the plan offers and how often it happens. Add a log so the manager records every session on the day it takes place. HR can then see whether the company kept its side of the plan.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Schedule the check-ins at a fixed interval, such as every 2 weeks, and choose who gets the reminder. Keep plan details out of email and chat. The reminder carries a link, and the goals stay behind the sign-in to the app.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give the employee a comments field and a signature at the start and at the close of the plan. Ask HR to read the wording of the template before the first plan goes out, and again whenever your policy changes.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Close each plan with an outcome
fields.howto_step_7_des: Record an outcome on every plan when it reaches its end date, such as goals met or plan extended. Note who made the decision and on what date. The record is then complete for anyone who reads it a year later.

faq_plan.q: What is a pip form template?
faq_plan.a: A PIP form template is a reusable form for a performance improvement plan. It records where the work falls short of the role, the goals that close the gap, the support the company offers, the check-in dates, and the date the plan ends.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a pip form template?
faq_plan.a: Describe the plan you run to Emergent's AI form builder, including how goals are measured and who signs. It builds the form and the HR view, and you change any part of it by prompting. Have HR read the wording before you send the first plan.

faq_plan.q: What sections should a PIP form template include?
faq_plan.a: Give it a section for each concern with dated examples, then the goals with a target and a due date, the support offered, the check-in schedule, and signatures from both people. End with an outcome field that someone fills in when the plan closes.

faq_plan.q: How do I write measurable goals in a PIP form template?
faq_plan.a: Name a number the employee controls and a date inside the plan. Answer more tickets is hard to judge at a check-in; close 30 tickets a week by the end of week 4 is not. Pull the number from the report you already use. Both people then read the same figure.

faq_plan.q: What plan length should a PIP form template use?
faq_plan.a: Set a length that fits at least 2 check-ins before each goal comes due, and treat the policy you follow as the outer limit. Put the end date on the form on day one. The HR view sorts every open plan by that date.

faq_plan.q: How do I send reminders from a PIP form template without employee details?
faq_plan.a: Send a reminder that says a check-in is coming and links to the plan, with nothing from the plan itself in the message. Emergent can build reminders by email or in Slack, and each one can carry only that link.

faq_plan.q: Can an employee add comments to a PIP form template?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you add the fields for it. A comments box when the plan opens and another when it closes puts the employee's view on the record next to the manager's. Ask both people to sign the same record.

faq_plan.q: How do I track every open plan from a PIP form template?
faq_plan.a: Keep each plan as a row with its end date and outcome, then sort by end date. Emergent builds the form and the dashboard on top of it from one prompt, and the rows sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a PIP form template record when the plan ends?
faq_plan.a: Record the outcome against each goal, the final result next to the target, who made the decision, and the date. Add a field for the next step, such as plan closed or plan extended, and a comments box for the employee.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free PIP form template I can change to fit my company?
faq_plan.a: Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a PIP form. Describe your own sections and check-in schedule, and the form follows them instead of a fixed layout.

plan.angle: The results for this query are downloadable Word, PDF and Excel PIP templates and HR guides that list the sections (the gap, the expected standard, goals, support, timeline, signatures). A file stops at the meeting. This page shows a working PIP form that keeps going after it: goals that will not save without a number and a date, the coaching the company promised logged as it happens, a reminder before each check-in that carries only a link, and an HR view of every open plan and its end date, all saved to a database the employer owns. No legal or HR-law advice; the copy gives instructions, not requirements.
